author: show-me state times
title: Gift from Rosen Family Foundation renames Mizzou's meat market
text:
The University of Missouri announced on April 29 that a donation from The Rosen Family Foundation will lead to the renaming of its student-run meat market as the “American Foods Group Meat Market at Mizzou.” The new name will take effect when the Michael L. Parson Meat Science Education and Training Laboratory opens this summer.
The change highlights a partnership between private philanthropy and public education, aimed at enhancing research, workforce development, and student experience in agriculture. The announcement was made during Gov. Mike Kehoe’s Beef Month Proclamation event at America’s Heartland Packing facility.
Bryon Wiegand, director of the Parson Meat Science Education and Training Lab and the Division of Animal Sciences in CAFNR, said, “This is a perfect example of public/private partnership that will benefit our state through shared priorities in applied research, industry‑driven innovation and workforce development. I am grateful to The Rosen Family Foundation for recognizing the importance of our meat market space for impactful student education and experience in meat processing; in turn, the space will educate future leaders for companies such as AFG that have come into our state and proven they truly are the food processing business for Missouri.”
David Jagodzinske, president and COO of American Foods Group, said, “American Foods Group appreciates the generosity of The Rosen Family Foundation and its support for the University of Missouri’s new meat laboratory and its continued commitment to charitable, educational and scientific purposes.” Missouri Director of Agriculture Chris Chinn added: “We are so proud to have American Foods Group in Missouri. The Rosen family truly cares about each of the communities where they have a presence. Their investment in the Michael L. Parson Meat Science Education and Training Laboratory is further proof of the family’s commitment to our state and to the future of the agriculture industry.”
Set to open in July just south of Trowbridge Livestock Center on campus, the Parson Meat Science Education and Training Laboratory aims to promote innovation through research while providing hands-on training using modern technology. Christopher Daubert, vice chancellor & dean at CAFNR said: “The Parson Meat Science Education and Training Lab and the American Foods Group Meat Market at Mizzou provide a new vision for meat processing to support our land-grant mission in teaching, research and extension activities – ultimately boosting economic value … This will truly be a state-of-the art hands-on space for student learning as well as a showcase for meat science. Thank you to AFG for joining us in this vision.”
University of Missouri College of Agriculture Food & Natural Resources (CAFNR) supports community development through education programs according to its official website. CAFNR functions as part of University System according to its official website, offers more than 50 undergraduate programs with students from across nation/world according to its official website, focuses on advancing agriculture/life sciences according to its official website, features competitive Division II athletics/Marching Musical Storm according to its official website.
